description: **A stroke width that is present is coerced, and only an absent one takes the default.** `boundStroke` opens `const sw = item.strokeWidth != null ? +item.strokeWidth : 1`, and the two halves of that read differently. `!= null` is the *only* route to the default, so a width that is present but is not a number does **not** fall back to 1 — it goes through `+`, JavaScript's coercion, and whatever that produces is what the mark is measured with. `+true` is 1, `+"3"` is 3, `+""` is **0**, and `+"wide"` is **NaN**. A width of 0 expands a mark by nothing and a width of NaN expands it by NaN, which then loses the comparisons `Bounds.union` is made of, so an unmeasurable symbol contributes nothing to the surface at all. This engine read the channel instead of coercing it — `asDouble`, then a `NaN` check that sent every non-number to the default — so all four of those measured as though the specification had said 1. `true` agreed by accident, which is why only the other three show. The symbols are spread along the row so each one's box is its own: `ten` and `three` are the controls that must still measure, `absent` and `explicitNull` are the two that must still take the default — and they are two cases, not one: `+null` is **0**, so a width written as `{"value": null}` reaches the default only through the `!= null` test and not through the coercion. A mutant that dropped that test survived a fixture holding `absent` alone, because an absent channel never reaches the coercion at all, and `blank`, `word` and `bool` are the coercions.
